source_text: 15 ∆ιὰ τί δὲ περὶ πολλοῦ ποιοῦνται δεικνύναι τὸν Χριστὸν ἄψυχον ἀνειληφέναι σῶμα, γεώδεις πλάττοντες ἀπάτας; Ἵνα εἰ δυνηθεῖεν ὑποφθεῖραί τινας, ταῦθ' οὕτως ἔχειν ὁρίζεσθαι, τηνικαῦτα τὰς τῶν παθῶν ἀλλοιώσεις τῷ θείῳ περιάψαντες Πνεύματι, ῥᾳδίως ἀναπείσωσιν αὐτοὺς, ὡς οὐκ ἔστι τὸ τρεπτὸν ἐκ τῆς ἀτρέπτου φύσεως γεννηθέν. 16 Σύμφωνα δὲ τούτοις διεξιὼν ὁ αὐτὸς Ἱερεμίας εἰσηγεῖται τὰς τοῦ Θεοῦ διακονούμενος φωνὰς, δι' ὧν δείκνυσιν, ὅτι μήτε τὰς τῶν δικαίων προσίεται πρεσβείας, εἰ βουληθεῖεν τῶν μιαιφόνων χάριν ἀξιῶσαι. Καὶ εἶπε Κύριος πρός με λέγων· Ἐὰν στῇ Μωϋσῆς καὶ Σαμουὴλ πρὸ προσώπου μου, οὐκ ἔστιν ἡ ψυχή μου πρὸς αὐτούς.
thought_title: Why the Arians deny Christ a soul
orientation: Eustathius is refuting the Arian claim that Christ took a soulless body, and here he explains their motive and then cites Jeremiah's words about God rejecting intercession for murderers.
pass_a_gloss: But why do they make much of showing that Christ took up a soulless body, fabricating earthy deceits? In order that, if they should be able to corrupt some people, to define that these things are so, then, having attached the alterations of the passions to the divine Spirit, they may easily persuade them that the changeable was not begotten from the unchangeable nature. And in agreement with these things, the same Jeremiah, going through them, introduces the voices of God which he serves, through which he shows that he does not receive the intercessions of the righteous, if they should wish to make request on behalf of murderers. And the Lord said to me, saying: If Moses and Samuel should stand before my face, my soul is not toward them.

choices.why: Keeps the adjective 'soulless' directly modifying 'body' as in the source, preserving the Arian claim being refuted.
rejected: assumed a body without a soul

choices.why: Literal rendering of the participle 'fabricating' with the adjective 'earthy' modifying 'deceits', matching the source's word order and force.

choices.term: τὰς τῶν παθῶν ἀλλοιώσεις τῷ θείῳ περιάψαντες Πνεύματι
choices.english: having attached the alterations of the passions to the divine Spirit
choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'passions' for παθῶν and 'Spirit' for Πνεύματι, and renders ἀλλοιώσεις as 'alterations' to keep the sense of change being attributed to the divine.
rejected: ascribing the changes of suffering to the divine Spirit
attaching the mutations of the passions to the Holy Spirit

choices.term: οὐκ ἔστι τὸ τρεπτὸν ἐκ τῆς ἀτρέπτου φύσεως γεννηθέν
choices.english: the changeable was not begotten from the unchangeable nature
choices.why: Uses the glossary terms 'changeable' and 'unchangeable nature', and keeps the passive 'was begotten' to preserve the Arian denial of the Son's generation.
rejected: what is mutable was not born of the immutable nature

choices.term: οὐκ ἔστιν ἡ ψυχή μου πρὸς αὐτούς
choices.english: my soul is not toward them
choices.why: Literal rendering of the Hebrew idiom via the Septuagint, keeping 'soul' as the glossary term and 'toward them' for πρὸς αὐτούς to preserve the sense of divine disfavor.

pass_b_english: Why, then, do they make so much of showing that Christ took up a soulless body, fabricating earthy deceits? So that if they are able to corrupt some people and get them to define the matter this way, they may then attach the alterations of the passions to the Spirit and easily persuade them that the changeable was not begotten from the unchangeable nature. Jeremiah, speaking in agreement with these things, introduces the voices of God which he serves, and through them shows that God does not accept even the intercessions of the righteous, if they should choose to plead on behalf of murderers. And the Lord said to me, saying, “If Moses and Samuel stood before my face, my soul is not toward them” (Jeremiah 15:1).
